findings.finding: The plan pins its verdict-bucket enumeration to `attest.compute_validity` as 'the enum source of truth', but B2's stated reader is `plan_review_status` (attest_gate.py), which wraps `claim_gate_check`. On the not-verified path `claim_gate_check` forwards `signing.verify_signature`'s verdict (attest_gate.py:124) and defaults to the literal `stale` (attest_gate.py:143). The signature-layer enum (types.py:261-271) includes `foreign_key`, `mismatch`, `key_not_valid_at_era`, `invalid`, `unavailable`, `unknown_kind` — none of which `compute_validity` emits and none of which appear in the plan's ACCEPTED/FLAG lists (only `unknown_scheme` is enumerated). The value vocabulary the criterion actually receives is therefore a superset of what the plan defines, and the pinned coverage test ('ACCEPTED ∪ FLAG = all non-error literals reachable from compute_validity') is anchored to the wrong function — it cannot enumerate the signature-layer verdicts the predicate really sees.
findings.location: Approach B2 ('pinned to attest.compute_validity as the enum source of truth'); Acceptance Criteria line 3 ('buckets the FULL enum per compute_validity')
scenarios: A bug fix whose plan-review attestation was signed by a foreign/rotated key -> plan_review_status returns `foreign_key` or `key_not_valid_at_era`, a verdict absent from all three enumerated buckets
Enum-growth coverage test written against compute_validity passes while the real signature-layer vocabulary drifts unnoticed
findings.suggested_fix: State that the enum source of truth is the union of compute_validity's verdicts, signing.verify_signature's verdict literal set (types.py PlanReviewSignatureResult), and claim_gate_check's `stale` default; classify every one of those literals into ACCEPTED/FLAG/INFRA; and assert the coverage test over that union.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and document the explicit bucket for the signature-authenticity verdicts (mismatch, foreign_key, key_not_valid_at_era, invalid) rather than letting them fall to fail-open INFRA — these are gate signal (FLAG/BLOCK), not infrastructure failures.
evidence: Plan: 'INFRA-FAIL-OPEN = {error} plus caught read/exception paths plus any verdict string in NEITHER list (future enum growth): emit a non-blocking advisory ... never BLOCK on infrastructure'
signing.py:460 `"verdict": "unknown_scheme"` and types.py:261-271 sibling verdicts `mismatch`/`foreign_key`/`invalid`/`key_not_valid_at_era` are signature-authenticity outcomes, not infra read errors
attest_gate.py:120-125 — any non-verified signature (including mismatch/foreign_key) returns that verdict verbatim to plan_review_status
findings.finding: The signature-integrity verdicts that reach the predicate — notably `mismatch` and `foreign_key` (and `key_not_valid_at_era`, `invalid`) — are never classified by the plan and so fall into the INFRA-FAIL-OPEN 'NEITHER list' bucket, silently failing OPEN (non-blocking advisory). These are tamper / signature-authenticity signals, not infrastructure read failures; treating them as fail-open means an oversized bug fix whose attestation fails signature verification (wrong key, corrupted/forged signature) passes the Gerrit gate with only an advisory. The plan never confronts this classification because it mis-identified the emitter and assumed only compute_validity's staleness verdicts are in scope.
findings.location: Approach B2 (INFRA-FAIL-OPEN = '...plus any verdict string in NEITHER list (future enum growth)')
scenarios: An oversized bug fix pushed with a tampered or foreign-key-signed plan-review attestation -> predicate sees `mismatch`/`foreign_key` -> unrecognized -> fail-open advisory instead of BLOCK
Key rotation past validity era -> `key_not_valid_at_era` -> silently advisory
findings.suggested_fix: Move signature-authenticity failures (mismatch, foreign_key, key_not_valid_at_era, invalid) into FLAG, and reserve INFRA-FAIL-OPEN strictly for `error`, caught read/exception paths, and genuinely unknown future literals.

Plan's residual rule: 'INFRA-FAIL-OPEN = {error} plus ... any verdict string in NEITHER list' — routes mismatch/foreign_key to fail-open advisory.
findings.finding: The plan enumerates the attestation verdict inventory (ACCEPTED/FLAG/INFRA-FAIL-OPEN) and pins it — plus the coverage test — to `attest.compute_validity` as 'the enum source of truth', but the B2 criterion reads `plan_review_status` (attest_gate.py:154), a strictly wider surface. `plan_review_status` wraps `claim_gate_check`, which on an unverified signature (attest_gate.py:120-125) forwards the raw `signing.verify_signature` verdict verbatim. That enum (types.py:261-271 / verify_signature_result.schema.json:17) includes `mismatch`, `foreign_key`, `key_not_valid_at_era`, `invalid`, `unavailable`, `unknown_kind` — literals `compute_validity` never emits and that the plan's ACCEPTED/FLAG lists omit (only `unsigned` and `unknown_scheme` overlap). The inventory was derived from the wrong symbol relative to the one actually consumed.
findings.location: Approach B2: 'Verdict buckets, pinned to attest.compute_validity as the enum source of truth' and AC line 'coverage unit test pins ACCEPTED ∪ FLAG = all non-error literals'
scenarios: Verdict `mismatch` (signature over tampered material) on an oversized bug fix: omitted from ACCEPTED/FLAG, falls to the residual INFRA-FAIL-OPEN rule → advisory only, never blocks — a real authenticity failure ships.
Verdict `foreign_key` / `key_not_valid_at_era` (signed by a non-trusted or era-invalid key): same silent fail-open on an oversized fix.

The coverage unit test, pinned to compute_validity, enumerates only compute_validity's literals, so it passes while these plan_review_status-reachable verdicts remain unbucketed — the 'enum growth surfaces as a failing test' guarantee does not hold for the signature-layer verdicts.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the signing verdicts {mismatch, foreign_key, key_not_valid_at_era, invalid, unavailable, unknown_kind} to FLAG (they mean the landing material is not covered by a trustworthy attestation), keep `error`/read-exceptions in INFRA-FAIL-OPEN, and rewrite the coverage AC to pin ACCEPTED ∪ FLAG against the literals reachable from `plan_review_status`/`claim_gate_check` (compute_validity ∪ verify_signature verdict enum), not compute_validity alone.

findings.suggested_fix: State that at review time the size signal is the explicit flag/count supplied to review-plan (B2 supplies the real diff count at Gerrit), and define the fallback behavior when no count is supplied (e.g. remain in the light advisory tier) so the trigger is deterministic.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the B1 scope label with the parent epic's decomposition: either update the parent's decomposition record from 'exemption narrowing' to 'extend the tier' (parent-first, per the conflict rule) or align the leaf, AND fix the plan's own file_impact ('claimability.py — narrow bug exemption to claim path') to match the body's 'the CLI claim-time bug exemption is untouched'.
evidence: Parent 2f4c session-log decomposition (5eb0-52a3-45f0-43e5): '24 (B: bug-fix plan review B1+B2) -> APPROVED -> ad0d' and child index 'ad0d bug-fix plan review (B1 exemption narrowing + B2 Gerrit DET backstop)'.

Plan B1: 'extend the bug review tier, not narrow an exemption ... The CLI claim-time bug exemption (rebar._commands.gates, claimability.py fast-fail table) is untouched — bugs stay claimable with no attestation.'
Plan file_impact contradicts the plan prose: 'src/rebar/llm/plan_review/claimability.py — narrow bug exemption to claim path' vs body 'exemption ... is untouched'.

Parent 2f4c authoritative AC: 'Explicit review-plan on a bug runs a real review, and the Gerrit backstop blocks oversized bug fixes lacking one' — does NOT require narrowing the claim-time exemption, so the leaf's 'extend, not narrow' framing remains a subset of the parent contract.
findings.finding: The leaf's B1 framing ('extend the bug review tier, NOT narrow an exemption'; 'The CLI claim-time bug exemption ... is untouched') is the verbal opposite of the parent epic's own decomposition record, which names this child 'B1 exemption narrowing' (session log 5eb0 decision-table entry 24 and the child index: 'ad0d bug-fix plan review (B1 exemption narrowing + B2 Gerrit DET backstop)'). The parent's authoritative ACs do not in fact require narrowing the claim-time exemption, so this is a label-level mismatch (incomplete_enumeration), not a contract contradiction — but it should be reconciled so the parent's decomposition and the leaf describe the same scope.
findings.location: Approach — B1 ('extend the bug review tier, not narrow an exemption'); Scope; file_impact entry 'claimability.py — narrow bug exemption to claim path'
scenarios: A reviewer or implementer tracing the parent epic's decomposition ('B1 exemption narrowing') against this plan sees an apparent scope reversal and cannot tell whether claimability.py is meant to change.

The plan's file_impact (claimability.py 'narrow bug exemption to claim path') is picked up by an escalation/size signal or by an implementer as authoritative, contradicting the body's 'untouched' and re-introducing the exemption-narrowing the body disowns.
findings.suggested_fix: Since the parent's authoritative ACs require only a real review + Gerrit backstop (not exemption narrowing), keep B1 as 'extend the tier', drop/relabel the claimability.py file_impact entry to reflect 'untouched', and update the parent epic 2f4c's session-log/child-index label from 'B1 exemption narrowing' to 'B1 bug-review-tier extension' so parent and leaf describe the same scope.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether B2's non-test classification reuses the existing test-path glob set ({**/test_*.py, **/*_test.py, tests/**} per code_review/criteria_routing.json + reviewers/index.json) or deliberately diverges; if divergent, justify why test_*.py / *_test.py outside tests/** count as non-test and reconcile the backtest FP count with the chosen rule.
evidence: Plan: 'a diff line is "test" iff its file path matches tests/** or conftest.py; everything else (src, scripts, workflows, docs) counts as non-test.'
Existing convention in src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json:109-119 ('tests' entry) classifies test files as {**/test_*.py, **/*_test.py, **/tests/**}.
Existing convention in src/rebar/llm/reviewers/index.json:62-73 ('tests' reviewer) uses the same glob set {**/test_*.py, **/*_test.py, tests/**}.

The plan's rule OMITS the name-based globs (test_*.py / *_test.py), so a src/foo/test_helpers.py or a top-level *_test.py would be counted as NON-test by B2 but as test by the established convention — a divergence on a rule the plan itself calls 'load-bearing for both the gate and the backtest'.
findings.finding: B2's non-test line classification rule ('a diff line is test iff its path matches tests/** or conftest.py') reinvents and NARROWS an existing, established test-path classification already used elsewhere in the codebase.
findings.location: Approach → B2, 'Non-test line classification rule'; AC line 'Non-test line classification rule stated and tested'
scenarios: A bug fix whose lines land in src/foo/test_helpers.py or a repo-root *_test.py: B2 counts them toward the >150 non-test threshold, potentially blocking a fix that is actually test-heavy — while the existing code-review 'tests' classifier would exclude them.
The 13-fix backtest FP count shifts depending on which classification is used, since the threshold predicate is line-count-sensitive.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse the existing test-path glob set (**/test_*.py, **/*_test.py, tests/**, plus conftest.py) so B2's classification matches the code-review 'tests' criterion rather than introducing a narrower tests/**-only rule.
